 Q2 & H1FY27 results: SAMHI delivers double-digit revenue growth as domestic demand drives occupancies 
 SAMHI Hotels Limited achieved a significant revenue growth of 15.6 percent year-on-year and a rise in occupancy rates. The company reported a RevPAR increase of 14.3 percent driven by domestic travelers. Additionally, the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio was around 3.1 times, indicating financial stability. Future growth is anticipated as new hotel openings are scheduled, including a W Hotel in Hyderabad. Online Bureau

 SAMHI Hotels Limited a branded hotel ownership and asset management platform in India, announced its unaudited standalone and consolidated results for the quarter and financial year ended September 30, 2026. Q2 FY27 — Key highlights —Strong same-store revenue growth of +12.6 percent YoY – ahead of our long-term guidance of 9 to 11 percent —Occupancy level at 78.6 percent (up from 75.0 percent Q2-FY26) —RevPAR growth of +14.3 percent YoY led by +9.2 percent ARR growth —Flow through of incremental EBITDA to incremental Revenue stood at around 57 percent —Domestic travellers constitute around 80 percent of total room nights we sold in the quarter. More resilient cohort given geo-political instability —Total Revenue growth of +15.6 percent YoY with comparable EBITDA growth of +21.3 percent YoY excluding impact of GST regulation change (not in base period Q2FY26) —Consolidated EBITDA margin of 39.1 percent (ex GST impact); 300 bps dilution due to GST impact resulting in reported margins at 36.1percent – scope for improvement in subsequent periods; growth in upscale inventory (not impacted by GST changes) to improve operating margins to around 40 percent —The on-going growth pipeline within our core portfolio and the progress in RARE India gives us a formidable path to growth —PBT (ex-exceptional items) a Rs. 53.4 crore (+39.9 percent YoY Reported) —PAT (ex-exceptional items) at Rs. 37.2 crore (+136.9 percent YoY Reported); Reported PAT includes exceptional gain of Rs. 3.9 crore and Rs. 84.1 crore in Q2FY27 and Q2FY26 respectively —Free Cash Flow at Rs. 82.7 crore —Effective Interest Rate at 7.8 percent (about 300 bps lower than IPO) —Net Debt-to-EBITDA at about 3.1x (about 2.2x on operating assets) Commenting on the performance, Ashish Jakhanwala , MD & CEO, SAMHI Hotels Ltd., said, “We are pleased to report our performance for the quarter. Occupancy held close to 80% and RevPAR grew by about 14 percent, making this a reassuring period for the business. Revenue growth remained ahead of our long-term guidance. Domestic travellers accounted for about 80 percent of the room nights sold during the quarter. This cohort has proven more resilient amid ongoing geopolitical instability, reinforcing our confidence in the resilience of the Indian economy and the opportunity it represents. “Against this strong backdrop, we have been steadily building for the future. For several quarters, our reported growth has been largely driven by same-store performance, as no new inventory came online. This is set to change. We look forward to opening the W Hotel in Hyderabad next fiscal year and have secured a pipeline of approximately 1,700 new rooms through FY2031. These initiatives put us on a path to strong growth, and our focus now is on delivering them on schedule. “We are equally proud of having built this pipeline without compromising our discipline: we add assets only in core markets and at a discount to replacement cost. We are not buying growth through expensive acquisitions; instead, we are building it through the efforts that conversions and turnarounds demand, as demonstrated in Bangalore, and by securing long-term leases, as in Noida and Hyderabad. “Our modest investment in RARE, together with ongoing discussions on a partnership with Marriott, will help RARE build a strong platform in experience-led leisure across the region, with limited capital exposure. “We expect H2 FY27 to be operationally stronger. Going forward, incremental EBITDA is expected to translate into free cash flow, with interest outflows remaining stable. This should enable us to increasingly fund future growth investments through internal cash generation, supporting a disproportionate improvement in free cash flow generation. “We released our first Sustainability Report for FY2025-26, covering 31 hotels and 4,899 rooms across 11 states. The report highlights improvements in energy efficiency, waste reduction and renewable energy usage. Building on our FY30 commitments, we will establish quantified targets across key sustainability parameters, with clear baselines to track and benchmark our progress”. Comments
